newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty buoyant despite c.bank buying.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty buoyant despite c.bank buying.

text.p: The Polish zloty closed flat against the currency basket as several waves of National Bank of Poland currency buying failed to dent in the zloty's armour.
Dealers said foreign inflows, which may be connected to the one billion zloty public offering of Bank Handlowy SA, pushed the zloty higher past resistance at 1.5 percent from parity.
"The central bank drained some $50-60 million today as foreign inflows created strong upward pressure on the zloty," said Tomasz Wolosz, senior dealer at BRE SA.
The zloty closed at 1.56/1.50 percent from the trading band after the central bank bought currencies between 1.54 and 1.50.
It closed at 3.2175/95 to the dollar, down from 3.2165/85 on Monday and at 1.8795/05 to the mark, up from 1.8780/90.
Dealers said the market's pro-zloty sentiment would remain intact on Wednesday as banks were likely to again test resistance levels amid a surplus of currencies on the market.
"The zloty may again test intervention levels as Tuesday's NBP buying did not weaken the unit, just kept it from gaining further," said Witold Wozniak of Deutsche Bank Polska SA.
Dealers said that foreign entry into Handlowy's IPO and foreign investor purchases of Polish bonds would probably keep the zloty buoyant in the near-future.
"Banks are testing the central bank because some believe that the road to two percent (from parity) can be opened," one dealer at a foreign bank in Warsaw said.
Dealers did not expect large foreign entry into Polish T-bills at Wednesday's additional 600 million zloty tender, at which yields are expected to hold flat or edge higher.
"If the minfin holds an additional T-bill tender it needs funds...which may mean investors will try for higher yields," said Robert Gluch, dealer at ING Bank in Warsaw.
Dealers said that the 39-week T-bill yields should rise to around 21.45 or 21.50 percent from 21.43 percent on Monday.
The average yield of the shorter 26-week T-bill should hold firm around 21.40 against last week's 21.37 percent.

"There should not be large demand for Polish paper from foreigners this week as many are still recovering from wounds caused by the fall of the Czech crown," said Maciej Kwiatkowski, dealer at Societe Generale in Warsaw.
